evidence.observation: get_parser builds a configargparse.ArgumentParser with default_config_files, config_file_parser_class=configargparse.YAMLConfigFileParser and auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_". This is what establishes the resolution ladder for every option: explicit CLI argument > environment variable (AIDER_*) > YAML config file > declared default, which is the contract this fixture is proving.

The fixture option --analytics (dest analytics) is declared with action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction and default=None. The BooleanOptionalAction supplies both --analytics and --no-analytics, and default=None makes it genuinely tri-state (None = unset/random, True, False). Because configargparse ranks the CLI above AIDER_ANALYTICS and above a config-file analytics: entry, an explicit --no-analytics must win over an env/config value of True, while no supplied value must leave the resolved value at None.

A second boolean, --auto-commits, is declared with BooleanOptionalAction and default=True. It demonstrates the 'unrelated default unchanged' half of the contract: overriding one option's tier must not perturb the declared defaults of options that received no input (auto_commits stays True unless explicitly negated).

setUp pins the environment for every TestMain case: it sets AIDER_ANALYTICS="false" (exercising the AIDER_* env tier of the fixture), sets OPENAI_API_KEY, redirects HOME to a temporary directory so no real ~/.aider.conf.yml leaks in, and swaps cwd to a temp dir. This makes env-tier vs config-tier vs CLI-tier resolution deterministic and shows the suite treats AIDER_ANALYTICS as a first-class input.

test_main_args pins the explicit-CLI-overrides-defaults behavior and the untouched-defaults invariant for booleans: --no-auto-commits yields auto_commits False, --auto-commits yields True, a bare main([]) yields auto_commits True and dirty_commits True, and --no-dirty-commits / --dirty-commits toggle only dirty_commits. It is the repository's own executable statement that an explicit CLI boolean is authoritative and that unrelated options keep their declared defaults.

test_true_vals_in_env_file writes .env with AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=on and asserts the resulting boolean reaches the coder as show_diffs True (with test_false_vals_in_env_file counterparting AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=off -> False). It proves the environment tier actually feeds boolean options, which is the tier an explicit CLI flag has to override.

claims.claim: The fixture --analytics is a tri-state boolean: argparse.BooleanOptionalAction plus default=None gives the three states None (unset), True (--analytics) and False (--no-analytics). This is what allows an explicitly supplied CLI value, including the negated form, to express a value distinct from 'unset'.

Aider's env and config tiers are wired in get_parser via auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_" and configargparse's YAML config-file parsing, so for the fixture the environment input is AIDER_ANALYTICS and the config input is an 'analytics:' key; configargparse resolves explicit CLI above env above config above the declared default.

An explicit CLI boolean is authoritative and unrelated options are left at their declared defaults: test_main_args asserts --no-auto-commits -> auto_commits False and --auto-commits -> True, while a no-flag invocation keeps auto_commits True and dirty_commits True, and the dirty-commits flags toggle only dirty_commits.

The environment tier genuinely supplies boolean option values (not only strings): test_true_vals_in_env_file / test_false_vals_in_env_file show .env AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=on|off resolving to show_diffs True|False, and TestMain.setUp pins AIDER_ANALYTICS=false for the fixture's own env tier.

Taken together, the args.py declaration and the test_main.py assertions specify the contract: for the tri-state --analytics, an explicit --no-analytics overrides AIDER_ANALYTICS=true (env) and 'analytics: true' (config), --analytics overrides an env/config False, an unset value stays None, and options that received no tier input retain their declared defaults.

conclusion: Contract established and demonstrated for the tri-state boolean option --analytics (aider/args.py:569-573) with its env/config tiers wired through get_parser's auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_" and YAML config parsing (aider/args.py:35-41). The resolution ladder is explicit CLI > environment (including .env loaded by main) > YAML config file > declared default. The executable demo .prale-eval/contract_demo.py passes: the source leg confirms the fixture is declared as BooleanOptionalAction with default=None, and the stdlib-argparse leg confirms the tri-state semantics, that an explicit --no-analytics overrides an inherited True, and that unrelated defaults (--auto-commits True, --dark-mode False, --pretty True) are unchanged; the repository's own test_main_args (tests/basic/test_main.py:263-290) independently pins the same override-and-untouched-defaults invariant. The only unverified leg is the end-to-end configargparse integration, because configargparse (and GitPython) are not installed in this environment and installing dependencies is out of scope; that limitation is recorded in result.json validation.notes and in the deliverable.
